audit.title: Managing CL Functions Subscriptions

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections open with usable leads: "You use a Chainlink Functions subscription to pay for, manage, and track Functions requests." Weak spot: step bodies defer to images, so a lifted chunk describes navigation without the actionable detail.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong: 8 sections, median 76 words, max 217, 0 level skips, sensible H2/H3 task boundaries. No tables/bullets, but numbered procedures suit the content.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 27 numerals but 0 carry units; most are step numbers. The genuinely useful specifics ("longer than five minutes," "0.1 LINK") are buried and sparse. No LINK fee amounts, no minimum balance, no network list, no contract addresses.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 5 links, 0 to primary sources, and one opaque "available [here]". No link to the FunctionsRouter contract reference or a canonical subscription concept page beyond the cancel guide.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Adequate. The subscription definition is liftable; the timeout rule ("time out requests that have been pending for longer than five minutes to unlock your subscription funds") is a good canonical statement.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Poor per measured facts: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, no og/twitter tags. Head could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm, but nothing was served.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 code blocks. This is a UI guide so full snippets aren't expected, but the page offers no CLI/SDK alternative and no copy-pasteable values, leaving agents nothing runnable.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Decent lifecycle: create → fund → add/remove consumer → cancel → timeout. Missing symptom/error phrasing ("request stuck pending," "can't cancel subscription in-flight requests") that devs actually query.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent product naming ("Chainlink Functions," "Subscription Manager"), unambiguous prose. No action needed beyond the image-dependency issue.

audit.summary: This is a task-oriented walkthrough for managing Chainlink Functions subscriptions (create, fund, add/remove consumers, cancel, time out requests) via the Subscription Manager UI. Its structure is clean — 8 headings, zero level skips, tight sections — but its single biggest GEO liability is that **the actual procedure lives in screenshots**: nearly every step is `(Image: Image)` with no textual description of the button, field, or value. Generative engines and coding agents can't read those images, so the retrievable text tells them *that* a step exists but not *what to do*. Combined with missing metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates) and no primary-source citations, the page under-delivers relative to best-in-class agent-ready docs.

recommendations.title: Convert screenshot-only steps to text-first instructions
recommendations.where: every `### Create/Fund/Add/Remove/Cancel` section and "Time out pending requests"
recommendations.issue: steps resolve to `(Image: Image)` with no textual action
recommendations.change: state the action in text before the image — e.g. "Click **Actions → Fund subscription**, enter the LINK amount (e.g. `0.1`), then confirm the MetaMask transaction." Keep images as supplements.
recommendations.why: engines cannot read images; text-first steps make each procedure retrievable and quotable — the largest single fidelity gain here.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased headings and an FAQ block
recommendations.where: near "Cancel a subscription" and "Time out pending requests"
recommendations.issue: the in-flight-request rule is buried in a Note; timeout is concept-titled
recommendations.change: add H3s like "Why can't I cancel my subscription? (in-flight requests)" and "My request is stuck pending — how do I time it out?"
recommendations.why: devs query by symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics with units
recommendations.issue: 0 numerals carry units; no fee/balance figures
recommendations.change: state minimum funding/balance requirements, LINK denomination, the 5-minute timeout threshold in a lead sentence, and the list of supported networks.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` schema with `dateModified`, set `<link rel="canonical">`, add a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured freshness/authority signals raise agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Fix opaque links and add primary-source references
recommendations.change: rename to "the [Functions Subscription Manager](https://functions.chain.link/)" and link the FunctionsRouter contract reference and a canonical subscriptions concept page.
recommendations.why: descriptive, authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a CLI/contract alternative for each UI action
recommendations.issue: no runnable path; only the UI is documented inline
recommendations.change: add a short fenced snippet (with function name and params) or a clear cross-link for cancelling/timing out via the FunctionsRouter contract.
recommendations.why: gives agents an executable path instead of image-only navigation.

antiPatterns: **Image-dependent walls with no alt text** — nearly every procedural step is `(Image: Image)`, invisible to text-based retrieval.
**Opaque link text** — "available [here]" (1 flagged in measured facts).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; confirm it lists this page.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical injection likely templated — verify by passing raw `<head>` to the CLI, since head metadata could not be captured here.
Image `alt` attributes are a site-template concern; populating them would partially mitigate the screenshot-dependency issue globally.
